ai.description: This 4–5 cm frog is lime green with scattered white spots and a cream belly. It features translucent, webbing-free fingers and distinct white-tipped toes. It inhabits high-altitude rainforests.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Rhacophorus calcadensis* is best distinguished by the distinct, large dark-brown blotches on its flanks and the granular texture of its belly skin.
ai.habitat: The Kalakkad tree frog inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kalakkad tree frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the canopy foliage near forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhacophorus calcadensis* breeds during the monsoon, depositing 50–100 eggs in foam nests attached to vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Kalakkad tree frog is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting evergreen forests at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kalakkad Tree Frog emits a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink-tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation near streams in its humid, evergreen forest habitat.
